To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for the Gaussian MIMO channel, we derive an upper bound and lower bound that are computable by convex programming; (ii) for the Rayleigh fading MIMO channel, the ergodic capacity can be characterized by a lower and upper bound, and the capacity can be met under certain conditions; (iii) for the Ray- leigh fading MIMO channel with all antennas of the same number at each node, the capacity is met under certain conditions

the ergodic capacity can be characterized for the MIMO relay channels over Rayleigh fading under certain regularity assumptions, and the ergodic capacity is achieved by certain schemes under some SNR conditions.
the capacity of the MIMORelay channel can be characterized exactly for certain channel conditions, and that this channel can be used for cooperative communications in wireless networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental capacity of the MISO/MIMO relay channel.
the characterization of the capacity of Gaussian and Rayleigh fading MIMO relay channels, and we present algorithms to compute upper bounds and lowerbounds on the ergodic channel capacity.
the characterization and computation of the capacity of MISO and MIMO relay channels with and without fading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ergodic capacity is achievable for a wide range of MIMO relay systems.
the capacity of the MIMORelay channel can be characterized exactly, which is a significant advance over the existing results.
the MIMO relay channels are more powerful than their single antenna counterparts, and that they are also more powerful than their multiple input single output (MISO) counterparts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a complete characterization of the capacity region for the Gaussian MIMO degraded relay channel, and have provided bounds for the ergodic capacity for the Gaussian MISO/MIMO relay channel over the Rayleigh fading channel.
the capacity of MISO relay channels is known exactly, while the capacity of MIMORelay channels is known only for the case where the number of antennas is equal at all nodes.
the capacity of a MIMO relay channel is determined by the channel conditions, SNR, and the number of antennas at the relay.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ergodic capacity is achievable in a MIMO relay channel, and therefore the MIMO relay can provide a capacity advantage over the single-input multiple-output (SIMO) relay.
the capacity of the MISO relay channel with fixed fading is equal to the capacity of a MISO broadcast channel, which is a surprising result.
the capacity of MIMORelay channels is very similar to that of the corresponding point-to-point MIMO channels.
